Prealgebra · Lesson 6.2

Solving Linear Equations

Solve this lesson →All lessons

An expression like 3x+53x+5 just describes a whole family of values, one for each xx. Put an equals sign between two expressions, like 3x+5=203x+5=20, and you make a claim that both sides come out to the same number. That claim is an equation, and the value of the variable that makes it true is a solution. Two pictures help through this lesson. The equals sign is the level beam of a two-pan balance, and the variable is wrapped in layers of operations that you take off one at a time.

Problem
A vending machine charges 33 tokens to wake up plus 55 tokens per snack, so ww snacks cost 5w+35w+3. One kid spent exactly 2323 tokens, giving 5w+3=235w+3=23. With no method yet, test whole numbers. At w=3w=3 the left side is 1818, at w=5w=5 it is 2828, so the answer sits between. The value that makes both sides equal is the solution. What whole number ww makes 5w+3=235w+3=23? Type that value.
Show a hint
  • You already passed 2323 between w=3w=3 (which gives 1818) and w=5w=5 (which gives 2828). The answer is the whole number sitting right between them, so test the one you skipped.
  • Try w=4w=4. Then 5w5w is 5×4=205×4=20, and 20+3=2320+3=23. That hits the target exactly, so that is your solution.
Show the full solution
Try w=4w=4. Then 5×4=205×4=20, and 20+3=2320+3=23, which is exactly the right side, so w=4w=4​. Testing values works here because the left side climbs by 55 each step, so once 2323 is bracketed between w=3w=3 and w=5w=5 only one whole number is left to check.
Problem
Before solving an equation you should be able to check one. Substituting means replacing every xx with a candidate and seeing whether both sides match. A note claims x=7x=7 solves 3x−5=193x−5=19, but 3(7)−5=16≠193(7)−5=16=19, so 77 fails. One of the values 77 or 88 actually solves 3x−5=193x−5=19. Type the value that works.
Show a hint
  • A correct solution must make the left side, 3x−53x−5, come out to exactly 1919. You already saw 77 gives 1616, which is too small, so test the other candidate.
  • Substitute x=8x=8. The left side becomes 3(8)−53(8)−5. Work out 3×8=243×8=24, then 24−524−5, and see whether you land on 1919.
Show the full solution
Substitute x=8x=8. The left side is 3(8)−5=24−5=193(8)−5=24−5=19, which matches the right side, so the value that works is 88​. The other candidate fails, since 3(7)−5=163(7)−5=16. Checking a value is always this direct, work out each side on its own and see whether they land on the same number.
Key idea
Solution and checking. An equation states that both sides are the same number. A solution is a value of the variable that makes that statement true. The identities from 6.1 held for every value, but an equation like 2x+5=112x+5=11 is true for only one value of xx. Always check a solution instead of trusting it. Put it back into the original equation, work out each side on its own, and compare. If both sides give the same number, your answer is a solution. If they do not, you made an error, almost always a dropped negative sign.
Fun fact
The equals sign was invented by Robert Recorde in 1557. He chose two parallel lines because nothing could be more equal. The symbol took about a century to become standard.
Problem
A thermos starts at tt degrees, the afternoon adds 1717, and the display settles at 99, so t+17=9t+17=9. The variable tt is sealed inside an add-1717 box. Lift those 1717 off the left pan, and lift the same 1717 off the right pan to keep the scale level. Solve t+17=9t+17=9 and type the value of tt.
Show a hint
  • The 1717 is added to tt. To undo an addition and free the variable, do the opposite operation to both sides at once. What single move strips that +17+17 off the left pan?
  • Subtract 1717 from both sides. The left pan becomes just tt, and the right pan becomes 9−179−17. That difference dips below zero, which is fine since the thermos started cold.
Show the full solution
Subtract 1717 from both sides. t+17=9t+17=9 t+17−17=9−17t+17−17=9−17 t=−8t=−8​ Checking, −8+17=9−8+17=9, which matches the right side. A negative answer is fine here, it just means the thermos started below zero.
Problem
Six identical sandbags, each of unknown mass mm, together tip a balance to 1515 units, so 6m=156m=15. The only thing wrapped around mm is a times-66, and division undoes multiplication, so divide both sides by 66 to leave one bag alone. The answer need not be a whole number, which is fine. Solve 6m=156m=15 and type mm as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The variable is multiplied by 66, so to peel that away you do the opposite of multiplying. Divide both sides of the equation by 66.
  • Dividing both sides by 66 gives m=156m=615​. Now reduce that fraction. Both 1515 and 66 share a factor of 33, so cancel it to reach lowest terms.
Show the full solution
Divide both sides by 66. 6m6=15666m​=615​ The left side leaves mm alone. On the right, 1515 and 66 are both divisible by 33, so 156615​ reduces and each sandbag has mass 5/25/2​ Checking, 6⋅52=302=156⋅25​=230​=15. A solution does not have to be a whole number.
Key idea
The balance rule. Doing the same thing to both sides of an equation does not change its solution. Adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing both sides by the same nonzero amount gives a new equation with the same answer. A two-pan balance behaves the same way, since equal changes to both pans keep the beam level. The forbidden move is changing one side and leaving the other alone, because that gives an equation with a different answer.
Problem
In 4x−9=74x−9=7, the variable sits inside two boxes, since it was multiplied by 44 first, then had 99 taken away. To unwrap, peel in reverse and pull the outer box off first, so add 99 to both sides, then divide by 44. Solve 4x−9=74x−9=7 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • The outer layer is the minus 99, so deal with it first. What can you add to both sides to undo subtracting 99?
  • Add 99 to both sides to get 4x=164x=16. Now the variable sits in only the times-44 box, so divide both sides by 44.
Show the full solution
Add 99 to both sides. 4x−9+9=7+94x−9+9=7+9 That gives 4x=164x=16, so divide both sides by 44. 4x4=16444x​=416​ x=4x=4​ The −9−9 came off first because it was the last thing done to xx. Checking, 4(4)−9=16−9=74(4)−9=16−9=7.
Problem
Start with nn, multiply by −3−3, then add 22, and you reach 1010, so −3n+2=10−3n+2=10. The times-−3−3 is the inner box and the add-22 is the outer box, so peel from the outside in. Subtract 22 first, then divide by −3−3. Watch the signs, because the answer will not be a whole number. Solve −3n+2=10−3n+2=10 and type nn as a fraction in lowest terms, including its sign.
Show a hint
  • The outer box is the +2+2, since the 22 was added last. Strip it off first by subtracting 22 from both sides, and see what is left on each side.
  • After subtracting, you have −3n=8−3n=8. The inner box is times −3−3, so undo it by dividing both sides by −3−3. A positive divided by a negative is negative, and 88 and 33 share no common factor, so it stays as a fraction.
Show the full solution
Subtract 22 from both sides to get −3n=8−3n=8, then divide both sides by −3−3. −3n−3=8−3−3−3n​=−38​ A positive over a negative is negative, and 88 and 33 share no common factor, so n=−8/3n=−8/3​. Checking, −3⋅(−83)=8−3⋅(−38​)=8 and 8+2=108+2=10. A negative fraction is a perfectly good solution.
Key idea
Isolating the variable. To isolate a variable is to get it alone on one side. Undo the operations around it in reverse order, the last one done first. A constant added on the outside comes off before the number multiplying on the inside. Each step is the opposite operation done to both sides, so the solution does not change. When the variable is alone, put your number back in and check that both sides agree.

Real equations are not always neat. Sometimes the variable's side holds several terms, like 2x+3x2x+3x, or a group that still needs distributing, like 4(t−7)4(t−7). Tidy that side first, using the like-terms and distributing work from 6.1, before you peel off a single layer. In every equation here the variable stays on one side and the other side is a plain number.

Problem
A delivery rider's day reads 5k+2+3k−7=195k+2+3k−7=19, where kk is the number of trips. Do not undo anything yet. First tidy the cluttered left side by combining like terms, exactly as in 6.1, then isolate kk. Solve 5k+2+3k−7=195k+2+3k−7=19 and type the value of kk.
Show a hint
  • Resist undoing anything first. The left side is a pile of like terms, so combine them before you touch the right side. Add up the kk terms, 5k5k and 3k3k, and separately add up the plain numbers, 22 and −7−7.
  • After combining you get 8k−5=198k−5=19, a clean two-step. Add 55 to both sides to get 8k=248k=24, then divide both sides by 88.
Show the full solution
Combine like terms on the left. The kk terms give 5k+3k=8k5k+3k=8k, and the plain numbers give 2−7=−52−7=−5. 8k−5=198k−5=19 Add 55 to both sides for 8k=248k=24, then divide both sides by 88. The rider made 33​ trips. Tidying first turns a four-term pile into a plain two-step equation, so there is less to keep track of.
Problem
A side can hide its real shape inside a group. In 6(2−q)=306(2−q)=30, the outer times-66 has to reach both pieces inside before anything else can happen, so it meets the 22 and the −q−q, and that minus sign rides along. Distribute carefully, then peel the two-step equation. Solve 6(2−q)=306(2−q)=30 and type the value of qq.
Show a hint
  • Hand the outer 66 to both pieces inside the group before you do anything else. The 66 hits the 22 and it also hits the −q−q, so watch that the sign rides along. The left side turns into 12−6q12−6q.
  • Now you have 12−6q=3012−6q=30, a plain two-step. Subtract 1212 from both sides to get −6q=18−6q=18, then divide both sides by −6−6. A positive divided by a negative is negative.
Show the full solution
Distribute the 66 across the group. 6(2−q)=306(2−q)=30 12−6q=3012−6q=30 Subtract 1212 from both sides to get −6q=18−6q=18, then divide both sides by −6−6. q=18−6=−3q=−618​=−3​ Checking, 2−(−3)=52−(−3)=5 and 6×5=306×5=30. The minus sign rides along when you distribute, so −q−q becomes −6q−6q, not 6q6q.
Problem
A paint mixer uses two thirds of a tank to fill today's order, so 23x=1032​x=10, where xx is the tank's capacity in liters. The variable is wrapped in a multiply-by-2332​ box, so multiply both sides by the reciprocal 3223​, which turns the 2332​ into a plain 11. Solve 23x=1032​x=10 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • The variable is being multiplied by 2332​. To undo a multiplication you do the opposite. Multiplying both sides by the reciprocal 3223​ will flip the 2332​ back to 11 and leave xx alone on the left.
  • Multiply both sides by 3223​. The left side becomes xx. The right side becomes 10⋅3210⋅23​, so work out 302230​.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by the reciprocal 3223​. 32⋅23x=32⋅1023​⋅32​x=23​⋅10 On the left, 32⋅23=123​⋅32​=1, leaving xx. On the right, 10⋅32=302=1510⋅23​=230​=15, so the tank holds 1515​ liters. Multiplying both sides by 33 and then dividing by 22 gets you the same place, since that is the same two moves.
Key idea
Simplify before you isolate. Clean up the side with the variable before you change both sides. Distribute any group with a number out front and gather every like term until that side is one variable term and one plain number. If the variable sits under a fraction bar, the denominator is the outermost layer, so clear it by multiplying both sides by that denominator. A fractional coefficient like 23x=832​x=8 comes off the same way, by multiplying both sides by the reciprocal, the fraction with numerator and denominator swapped. Both moves are done to both sides, so the answer does not change.
Problem
Solving for the variable is often just the first half of a question. A ticket booth's group passes xx satisfy 5(x−2)=355(x−2)=35, but the manager wants the wristband count, given by 2x+12x+1. First solve 5(x−2)=355(x−2)=35 for xx, then compute 2x+12x+1. Type that final number.
Show a hint
  • Start by solving for xx on its own. The whole left side is multiplied by 55, so undo that first by dividing both sides by 55. Set the value of xx aside, because the question is really asking about 2x+12x+1.
  • Dividing both sides by 55 gives x−2=7x−2=7, so adding 22 to both sides gives x=9x=9. Now substitute into the wristband rule. Work out 2×9+12×9+1 and type that single number.
Show the full solution
Divide both sides by 55 to get x−2=7x−2=7, then add 22 to both sides for x=9x=9. The question wants the wristband count, so substitute into 2x+12x+1. 2(9)+1=18+1=192(9)+1=18+1=19 The booth hands out 1919​ wristbands. Solving for the variable was only half the job, so reread what the question actually asks for before typing an answer.
Problem
Sometimes you are handed the variable and must hunt for a missing number. A game designer's win happens when a score xx satisfies 3x+c=203x+c=20, where cc is a fixed bonus she still has to choose. She wants x=4x=4 to count as a win, which means x=4x=4 must be a solution. Substitute 44 for xx, then solve for cc. Type the value of cc.
Show a hint
  • You know what xx is this time, so put it to work. A solution is a value that makes the equation true, so replace xx with 44 in 3x+c=203x+c=20 and see what the equation turns into.
  • After substituting you get 12+c=2012+c=20. Now cc is the only unknown left, sitting on one side. Undo the +12+12 by subtracting 1212 from both sides.
Show the full solution
Substitute 44 in for xx, since x=4x=4 has to make the equation true. 3(4)+c=203(4)+c=20 12+c=2012+c=20 Subtract 1212 from both sides. c=8c=8​ Checking, 3(4)+8=12+8=203(4)+8=12+8=20. Nothing new is going on here. The letter you solve for is just whichever one is still unknown.
Problem
A community garden shares a total across 44 equal plots, ending with 66 beds each, so 3(m−2)+2m4=643(m−2)+2m​=6, where mm is beds per row. Peel the outermost box first by multiplying both sides by 44, then distribute, combine like terms, and isolate mm. Solve 3(m−2)+2m4=643(m−2)+2m​=6 and type the value of mm.
Show a hint
  • The whole left side is wrapped in a division by 4. That is the outermost box, so undo it first. Multiply both sides by 4 to clear the denominator, and the equation becomes 3(m−2)+2m=243(m−2)+2m=24.
  • Now distribute the 3 across m−2m−2 to get 3m−63m−6, then add the 2m2m. The like terms 3m3m and 2m2m combine into 5m5m, so the left collapses to 5m−6=245m−6=24. Add 6 to both sides, then divide both sides by 5.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 44 to clear the denominator. 3(m−2)+2m=243(m−2)+2m=24 Distribute the 33, then combine the like terms 3m3m and 2m2m. 3m−6+2m=243m−6+2m=24 5m−6=245m−6=24 Add 66 to both sides for 5m=305m=30, then divide both sides by 55. m=6m=6​ The denominator was the outermost layer, so it had to come off before there was anything to tidy inside. Checking, 3(4)+12=243(4)+12=24 and 24÷4=624÷4=6.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A diver's instrument reads higher as she rises, and her start reading xx satisfies x+12=5x+12=5, where negative values mean below the surface. Solve x+12=5x+12=5 and type the value of xx.
Show the solution
Subtract 1212 from both sides. x+12=5x+12=5 x+12−12=5−12x+12−12=5−12 x=−7x=−7​ Checking, −7+12=5−7+12=5, which matches the right side. Landing below zero is fine, it just means she started below the surface.
Practice
A jar holds some marbles, and after 66 more are dropped in it holds 2020. With nn the starting count, that is n+6=20n+6=20. Solve for nn and type the value.
Show the solution
Subtract 66 from both sides. n+6−6=20−6n+6−6=20−6 n=14n=14 The jar started with 1414​ marbles. Checking, 14+6=2014+6=20.
Practice
Four identical packs together hold 99 mini sets, so 4m=94m=9, where mm is how many fit in one pack. Solve for mm and type the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Divide both sides by 4, which gives m=94m=49​. Since 9 and 4 share no common factor, that is already in lowest terms, so 9/49/4​. Checking, 4⋅94=94⋅49​=9.
Practice
A descending drone's tracker satisfies −6y=54−6y=54. Divide both sides by −6−6 to solve. Type the value of yy, including its sign.
Show the solution
Divide both sides by −6−6. That leaves yy on the left, and on the right 5454 divided by 66 is 99, while a positive divided by a negative is negative. So y=−9y=−9​. Checking, −6×(−9)=54−6×(−9)=54, which matches the right side.
Practice
A vending machine charges xx per snack plus a flat $7$7 fee, and 33 snacks come to $22$22, so 3x+7=223x+7=22. Peel the constant, then the coefficient. Solve and type the value of xx.
Show the solution
Subtract 77 from both sides. 3x+7−7=22−73x+7−7=22−7 3x=153x=15 Then divide both sides by 33. x=5x=5​ Checking, 3(5)+7=15+7=223(5)+7=15+7=22. The constant comes off before the coefficient, because adding the 77 was the last thing done.
Practice
A baker uses ww cups on each of two trays and sets aside 33, using 44 cups in all, so 2w−3=42w−3=4. Add 33 to both sides, then divide by 22. Type ww as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Add 3 to both sides to get 2w=72w=7, then divide both sides by 2. Each tray takes 7/27/2​ cups. Checking, 2⋅72=72⋅27​=7 and 7−3=47−3=4, which matches the right side.
Practice
Tidy the busy left side first, then hunt for the value. Solve 7t−2−4t+5=187t−2−4t+5=18 and type the value of tt.
Show the solution
Combine like terms on the left. The tt terms give 7t−4t=3t7t−4t=3t, and the numbers give −2+5=3−2+5=3. 3t+3=183t+3=18 Subtract 33 from both sides for 3t=153t=15, then divide both sides by 33. t=5t=5​ Checking, 7⋅5−2−4⋅5+5=35−2−20+5=187⋅5−2−4⋅5+5=35−2−20+5=18.
Practice
Five identical kits each ship with 44 items missing, so each holds d−4d−4, and all five total 1515, giving 5(d−4)=155(d−4)=15. Distribute the 55 first, then isolate dd. Type the value of dd.
Show the solution
Distribute the 5 across the parentheses. 5(d−4)=155(d−4)=15 5d−20=155d−20=15 Add 20 to both sides for 5d=355d=35, then divide both sides by 5. d=7d=7​ Checking, each kit holds 7−4=37−4=3 items, and five kits hold 5⋅3=155⋅3=15.
Practice
A triangle has three equal edges, each measuring 2k+52k+5, and its perimeter is 99, so 3(2k+5)=93(2k+5)=9. Distribute, then solve. Type the value of kk.
Show the solution
Distribute the 33 across the group. 3(2k+5)=93(2k+5)=9 6k+15=96k+15=9 Subtract 1515 from both sides for 6k=−66k=−6, then divide both sides by 66. k=−1k=−1​ Checking, each edge is 2(−1)+5=32(−1)+5=3, and three edges of 33 give a perimeter of 99.
Practice
Three fifths of a tank's capacity xx comes to 99 liters, so 35x=953​x=9. Multiply both sides by the reciprocal 5335​ to free xx. Type the value of xx.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by the reciprocal 5335​. 53⋅35x=53⋅935​⋅53​x=35​⋅9 The two fractions cancel to 11 on the left, and on the right 53⋅9=453=1535​⋅9=345​=15, so x=15x=15​. Checking, 35⋅15=455=953​⋅15=545​=9.
Practice
A fractional coefficient scales bb, and the other side is negative, so 27b=−472​b=−4. Free bb by multiplying both sides by the flipped fraction 7227​, carrying the negative through. Type the value of bb.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by the reciprocal 7227​. 72⋅27b=72⋅(−4)27​⋅72​b=27​⋅(−4) The left side collapses to bb, and the right side is −2822−28​, so b=−14b=−14​. Checking, 27⋅(−14)=−287=−472​⋅(−14)=7−28​=−4. The minus sign carries straight through the multiplication.
Practice
A value 3h+23h+2 shared equally among 44 display cases gives 55 each, so 3h+24=543h+2​=5. Undo the division first by multiplying both sides by 44, then solve. Type the value of hh.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 44 to clear the denominator. 3h+2=203h+2=20 Subtract 22 from both sides for 3h=183h=18, then divide both sides by 33. h=6h=6​ Checking, 3⋅6+2=203⋅6+2=20 and 204=5420​=5. The denominator is the outermost layer, so it comes off before anything on the top.
Practice
A quantity 5x+25x+2 divided into 44 equal parts gives 66 each, so 5x+24=645x+2​=6. Clear the denominator first by multiplying both sides by 44, then solve. Type xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 44 to clear the denominator. 5x+2=245x+2=24 Subtract 22 from both sides for 5x=225x=22, then divide both sides by 55. x=22/5x=22/5​ Since 2222 and 55 share no common factor, that is already in lowest terms. Checking, 5⋅225+2=245⋅522​+2=24 and 244=6424​=6.
Practice
You are told n=5n=5 is a solution of 2n+c=172n+c=17, so plugging in 55 must make it true. Substitute n=5n=5, then solve for the constant cc. Type the value of cc.
Show the solution
Substitute 5 in for nn, since n=5n=5 has to make the equation true. 2(5)+c=172(5)+c=17 10+c=1710+c=17 Subtract 10 from both sides. c=7c=7​ Checking, 2(5)+7=10+7=172(5)+7=10+7=17, which matches the right side.
